title: Sales processes, forecasting, territories, activities, and pipeline reporting
objectives: Explain a Sales Process as the Stage picklist subset tied to Opportunity record types, not as a Flow.
Map Opportunity Stage to Forecast Category and Probability, and say when a user override is allowed.
Contrast role-hierarchy Collaborative Forecasts with Enterprise Territory Management territory rollups.
Place Activities (tasks/events) and pipeline reports on the Opportunity without treating a report as the forecast engine.
diagnostic_question: Leadership wants next-quarter revenue, West-region ownership, and a weekly call plan. Which of sales process, forecast category, territory model, activities, or a pipeline report do you configure first, and what evidence would change that?
definition: After APP-001's objects exist, this lesson is how deals move and how leadership sees them: a Sales Process controls which Opportunity Stages a record type may use; those Stages map to Forecast Category and Probability for Collaborative Forecasts; Enterprise Territory Management can roll forecasts by territory instead of the user role hierarchy; Activities are the work on the deal; pipeline reporting inspects Opportunity data rather than replacing forecasts. ([Stage to Forecast Category](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.faq_forecasts_category_mapping.htm); [ETM with Collaborative Forecasts](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000387713); [Territory assignments for splits](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.teamselling_set_up_territory_for_oppty_splits_product_splits.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers listen for whether you know Stage is not Forecast Category, whether Closed Lost is Omitted, and whether territories are not the role hierarchy. A pretty pipeline report that ignores forecast mappings and overlays will not match the Forecasts tab.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a sports league season. The Sales Process is the rulebook of legal game phases (Stages) for that division's record type. Forecasting is the scoreboard projection: each phase maps to Pipeline, Best Case, Commit, Closed, or Omitted. Territories are home regions, not the coaching org chart. Activities are practices and games on the calendar. Pipeline reporting is the standings page—it reads the games; it is not the scoreboard engine.
deeper_explanation: Forecasts rely on how Opportunity Stage picklist values map to Forecast Category. If Negotiation/Review maps to Commit, those amounts sit in Commit. If Stage changes, probability and forecast category also change. Closed Lost maps to Omitted and is not included in forecasts. ([Stage to Forecast Category](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.faq_forecasts_category_mapping.htm))

Users who own the Opportunity can edit Forecast Category and override the default stage-to-category mapping. In Lightning Experience, all forecast categories are available for all stages; Classic is more restrictive. Update mappings on Opportunity Stage in Object Manager. ([Stage to Forecast Category](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.faq_forecasts_category_mapping.htm))

Enterprise Territory Management and Collaborative Forecasts can be combined so forecast managers see rollups by territory hierarchy rather than the standard user role hierarchy. Enable ETM, then enable Territory Forecasts in Forecast Settings, and assign a forecast manager per territory. ([ETM with Collaborative Forecasts](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000387713))

Territory models, types, and the Manage Territories permission are metadata. Opportunity rows and activities are data. Opportunity Splits can be assigned to territories so matrixed teams forecast split amounts. ([Territory assignments for splits](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.teamselling_set_up_territory_for_oppty_splits_product_splits.htm))

Activities (tasks and events) record work against the Opportunity; they do not change Forecast Category by themselves. Pipeline reports and dashboards inspect Opportunity Stage, Amount, Close Date, and owner/territory—useful, but they are not Collaborative Forecasts submissions or manager judgment.

mental_model.analogy: A sports league season: Sales Process = division rulebook of legal phases; Stage = which phase this game is in; Forecast Category = how that phase counts on the projected scoreboard; Territory = home region; Role hierarchy = coaching org chart; Activities = practices and fixtures; Pipeline report = published standings.
useful_mapping: Sales Process + record type → which Stage values the rep may pick
Stage → default Probability and Forecast Category
Forecast Category override → rep judgment on this Opportunity
Collaborative Forecasts on roles → rollup up the coaching chart
Territory Forecasts → rollup up home regions instead
Activity → a scheduled practice or game, not the score
Pipeline report → standings query, not the official forecast submission
where_it_breaks: A user can override Forecast Category so Stage and scoreboard disagree.
Territories do not replace sharing or role hierarchy unless you design them to.
Reports can filter differently from the Forecasts tab (date, product family, splits).
The analogy does not encode Einstein Forecasting or quota upload mechanics.

teach_back_prompt: Explain why two Opportunities in the same Stage can appear in different forecast categories, then name one reason a pipeline report still disagrees with the Forecasts tab.

review_schedule.prompt: Recite Stage versus Forecast Category and what Omitted means.
Choose sales process, territory model, forecast type, activity, or report for five stakeholder asks.
Draw role-hierarchy forecasts versus territory forecasts.
Diagnose Commit that does not match the Stage mapping.
Two-minute interview: process, forecast, territory, activity, report.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: A Sales Process limits Stages for a record type. Stages map to Forecast Category. Owners can override category. Forecasts roll up by role hierarchy unless Territory Forecasts use ETM. Activities log work. Pipeline reports inspect deals; they are not the Forecasts tab.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I start from the question. Wrong Stages? Sales Process and record type. Wrong bucket? Stage mapping, then owner override, then LEX vs Classic. Geography vs manager chart? ETM plus Territory Forecasts and a forecast manager per territory. Team credit? Splits and Split Territory. 'Did we call them?' is an Activity, not a new Stage. I never promise a report will match Collaborative Forecasts without checking date, splits, and overlays.

terminology.plain: The allowed Opportunity Stages for a given record type.
terminology.precise: Metadata that subsets the Stage picklist. Different teams (new business vs renewal) get different processes. It is not a Flow and not a forecast type.
terminology.example: LAB_NewBusiness process omits Renewal Negotiation stages.
terminology.non_example: A record-triggered Flow that stamps Stage.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Path: the Lightning coaching UI on those stages, not the process itself.
terminology.boundary: Path and Kanban settings are neighboring UI, not the process definition.

terminology.plain: The bucket that decides how this Opportunity counts in Collaborative Forecasts.
terminology.precise: Mapped from Stage (Pipeline, Best Case, Commit, Closed, Omitted). Closed Lost is Omitted. Owners may override. LEX allows all categories on all stages.
terminology.example: Stage Negotiation/Review mapped to Commit unless the owner moves it to Best Case.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Probability: a related percentage on Stage, not the forecast bucket.
terminology.boundary: Einstein win scoring is a different feature.

terminology.plain: The official forecast rollup product on the Forecasts tab.
terminology.precise: Rolls opportunity amounts (or quantities/splits) up a hierarchy—user roles by default, or territories when Territory Forecasts are enabled. Includes manager judgment and optional submissions in current Help.
terminology.example: West VP sees rolled Commit for the quarter from direct reports or territories.
terminology.non_example: A joined report of Open Opportunities labeled 'the forecast.'
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Pipeline report: inspection tool, not the forecast engine.
terminology.boundary: Quota and forecast type configuration: reverify in Forecast Settings.

terminology.plain: A model of sales regions and who covers them, separate from the role hierarchy.
terminology.precise: Territory types, models, and territories. Can drive sharing and, with Collaborative Forecasts, territory-based forecast rollups. Configuring territories requires Manage Territories.
terminology.example: LAB_West-Coast territory on an active model assigned to Account LAB_Northwind.
terminology.non_example: Renaming a User Role 'West Coast' and calling it a territory.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Role hierarchy: manager chain used by default forecasts and some sharing.
terminology.boundary: Original Territory Management (legacy) is not this product; do not mix names.

terminology.plain: A task or event logged against people and deals.
terminology.precise: Work records. They do not by themselves change Forecast Category. Deeper email/calendar/mobile behavior is APP-005.
terminology.example: Event LAB_Discovery Call related to Opportunity LAB_Northwind Q3.
terminology.non_example: Changing Stage to Qualification because 'we called them' without logging work.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Chatter post: collaboration, not a due-dated task (APP-005).
terminology.boundary: This lesson only needs activities as pipeline hygiene, not Inbox setup.

terminology.plain: Reports and dashboards that inspect open and closed Opportunities.
terminology.precise: Queries on Opportunity fields (Stage, Amount, Close Date, owner, territory). Useful for inspection. Not a substitute for Collaborative Forecasts mappings, overlays, or submissions.
terminology.example: LAB_Open Pipeline by Stage report filtered this fiscal quarter.
terminology.non_example: The Forecasts tab Commit column copied into Excel and called a report definition.
terminology.boundary: Report types and row-level security are DATA/SEC topics.

terminology.plain: A way to share credit (and sometimes forecast) across a selling team.
terminology.precise: Splits can be assigned to territories so matrixed teams forecast appropriate amounts. Requires enabling splits and adding Split Territory on layouts when using territories.
terminology.example: AE 60% / SE 40% revenue split on LAB_Northwind Q3, each with a Split Territory.
terminology.non_example: Two duplicate Opportunities for the same deal.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Account Team: coverage on the Account, not opportunity credit.
terminology.boundary: Overlay vs revenue split types: confirm labels in the org.

terminology.plain: The forecast bucket that means 'do not count this deal.'
terminology.precise: Closed Lost maps to Omitted and is not included in forecasts. Other stages can be mapped to Omitted if the business truly wants them out.
terminology.example: Closed Lost LAB_deal disappears from Commit/Pipeline totals.
terminology.non_example: Deleting the Opportunity so it 'will not forecast.'
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Closed: won revenue in the forecast, not omitted.
terminology.boundary: Custom mappings belong on the Stage picklist, not a formula field.

when_to_use: When different selling teams need different Opportunity Stages via a Sales Process and record type.
When Collaborative Forecasts must bucket deals using Stage to Forecast Category mappings, including Omitted for Closed Lost.
When forecast rollups should follow Enterprise Territory Management regions rather than the user role hierarchy.
When managers need Activities on the deal and pipeline reporting to inspect Opportunities without replacing the Forecasts tab.
when_not_to_use: Do not use a pipeline report as a substitute for Collaborative Forecasts mappings, overlays, or submissions.
Do not treat User Roles as territories, or skip Manage Territories when you actually need ETM.
Do not add extra Stages to 'track a phone call' when the need is an Activity.
Do not assume Lightning Forecast Category overrides behave like Salesforce Classic restrictions.

interview_questions.question: How do Sales Processes, Stages, and Forecast Categories fit together?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A Sales Process subsets Stages for a record type. Each Stage maps to Probability and Forecast Category. Collaborative Forecasts buckets deals from that category, unless the owner overrides it.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not treat Stage and Forecast Category as synonyms. Closed Lost is Omitted in Help's example. Lightning lets owners pick any category; Classic restricts by stage. A pipeline report that groups by Stage can still disagree with the Forecasts tab because of overrides, dates, and splits. Sales Process is metadata; the Opportunity row is data.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Renewal process hides Prospecting; Negotiation maps to Commit unless the AE marks Best Case.
tradeoffs: One process vs many record types

interview_questions.question: When do you use territories instead of the role hierarchy for forecasts?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When leadership needs geographic or overlay rollups. Enable ETM, then Territory Forecasts, and put a forecast manager on each territory. Do not rename roles and call them territories.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Default Collaborative Forecasts follow user roles. Help describes integrating Enterprise Territory Management so rollups follow the territory tree. Splits can carry Split Territory for matrixed credit. I check Manage Territories permission and edition. Sharing impact is a security conversation, not a free gift of ETM.
interview_questions.example: LAB_West territory forecast manager sees West Commit; the AE's manager chain is ignored for that forecast type.

interview_questions.question: VP says the dashboard Commit is the forecast. How do you respond?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A pipeline dashboard inspects Opportunities. Collaborative Forecasts uses Stage mappings, overlays, and hierarchy. I reconcile filters before changing mappings.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I compare close-date windows, won/lost, product families, splits, and Omitted. I check owner Forecast Category overrides. I offer to align the report to forecast categories if they want inspection, but I will not silently replace the Forecasts tab. Activities explain hygiene, not the number.
interview_questions.example: Dashboard includes Closed Lost; Forecasts omits it—totals differ on purpose.

interview_questions.question: Sales wants a Stage called 'Left Voicemail' for forecasting.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I push back. That is an Activity. Extra Stages change probability and Forecast Category mappings for every deal that uses them.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I show the Stage mapping table. I propose a Task type or a field plus Path guidance. If they truly need a process phase, we add it to the right Sales Process only and map it deliberately (usually Pipeline). I do not pollute renewal and new-business alike.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Discovery Event logged; Stage stays Qualification mapped to Pipeline.

interview_questions.question: Negotiation is mapped to Commit but the deal is Best Case. Diagnose.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Check the owner's Forecast Category override. In Lightning they can pick any category. Then check forecast type and date.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I open the Opportunity. If Forecast Category was edited, that is working as documented, not a mapping bug. I look at Classic vs LEX. I check whether we are on quantity or product-family forecasts. I do not remap Stage globally to chase one deal.
interview_questions.example: AE moved LAB_Northwind Q3 from Commit to Best Case before a legal review.
tradeoffs: Training vs removing FLS on the field
follow_ups: How do submissions freeze a snapshot?

interview_questions.question: West forecast is empty after 'setting up territories.'
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Confirm ETM is actually enabled, Territory Forecasts is on, a forecast manager exists, and opportunities are assigned to those territories.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: City-named roles are not territories. I verify the model is active, account/opp assignment rules ran, and the user has Forecasts access. Splits without Split Territory still forecast on the wrong slice. I treat sharing symptoms separately from forecast rollup.
interview_questions.example: Roles renamed West; Enable Territory Forecasts never clicked.

interview_questions.question: When would you avoid Enterprise Territory Management for this forecast problem?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When the org really forecasts by manager chain, edition cannot support ETM, or the pain is only a report filter. ETM is a data-model change, not a dashboard widget.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I weigh sharing impact, assignment-rule maintenance, and Manage Territories ownership. If they need overlay splits, I may still use splits on roles without full territory forecasts. I will not enable ETM to color a report. I also will not fake territories with Account picklists if they asked for Collaborative Forecasts rollups.
interview_questions.example: Five-person startup with one VP: keep role-based Collaborative Forecasts.
weak_answer_warnings: Enabling ETM as a report trick

interview_questions.question: Teach this topic with a concrete analogy and where it breaks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: League season: Sales Process is the division rulebook, Stage is the game phase, Forecast Category is the scoreboard bucket, territories are home regions, roles are the coaching chart, activities are fixtures, reports are standings.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: It breaks when a captain overrides the bucket, when standings filters disagree with the official scoreboard, and when painting 'West' on a coach's badge does not create a home region. I then cite Help: Closed Lost omitted, LEX overrides, ETM plus Territory Forecasts. I keep APP-001 objects out of the way except as the deal being scored.
interview_questions.example: Whiteboard: one deal, mapped Commit, owner flips Best Case, report still shows Stage Negotiation.
follow_ups: Where do activities hang for mobile? (APP-005)
weak_answer_warnings: Generic catalog metaphors instead of the league-season mapping
